clue.text: A revolutionary form of torture once

definitions.meaning: something that revolves, turning round and round on an axle
breaking on the ... was a medieval method of execution and torture

explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turns on its axis, and victims were once broken on a wheel as a punishment.

clue.text: Determination of western king to fetter hostile prisoner

indicators.note: to fetter means the outer pieces bind the others, chaining them inside

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, a king's royal cipher
ill as in ill will, hostile or unfriendly
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A resolute western monarch shackles an unfriendly captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fetter' means binding round. ER usually stands for the Queen, but it can also be Edwardus Rex, King Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Willpower is strength of resolve, the drive to see something through.

clue.text: Divorcee takes up painting as an additional subject

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, takes up means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: painting is art

explanation.surface: A divorced partner takes up painting as an extra subject to study.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'takes up' reads ART upwards, giving TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something added on, beyond what is usual or required.

clue.text: Greedy person passing his tongue over his fudge

parts.note: a licker is someone who passes their tongue over something

indicators.note: to fudge is to fiddle or fake, so the second his is rearranged

explanation.surface: A greedy fellow licks his lips over a piece of fudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fudge' looks like the sweet being licked, but it is a verb meaning to fiddle, rearranging the second HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lickerish is an archaic word meaning eager or greedy, especially for food or pleasure.

clue.text: Thrifty management restricting American players? Hard lines

indicators.note: the hard lines hem in the American players, holding them within their bounds

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines of track
a band is a group of musical players

explanation.surface: A frugal manager keeps American musicians on a tight budget, and they grumble about their hard luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard lines!' reads as a sigh of sympathy, but here it supplies letters, and 'restricting' puts them around the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is the careful, economical running of resources, as in a farm or household.

clue.text: Arkwright's son raised food in Germany

parts.note: Noah built the ark, and Ham was one of his sons

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word for food is written upwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: The son of a millwright grew food while living in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arkwright' looks like the inventor Richard Arkwright, but it is Noah, the ark builder. In a down entry 'raised' turns GRUB upwards to BURG.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamburg is a major port city in northern Germany, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Fanciful dreams of shaking off a state of bondage

indicators.note: fanciful means the two words are freely rearranged
shaking off means the letter a is dropped from the mix

explanation.surface: Imaginative dreams of throwing off slavery.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of DREAMS OF, remove the A ('shaking off a'), and rearrange the rest ('Fanciful').
explanation.definitionFit: Serfdom was the medieval condition of a peasant bound to the land and their lord.

clue.text: A voting system one politician put together in thirty days

parts.note: PR is proportional representation
I is the Roman numeral one
L stands for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A voting reform and a lone politician are combined within a month.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Thirty days hath September, April, June and November' lists the months with thirty days.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month of the year has thirty days, as the old rhyme says.

clue.text: Release round about half the capital for the contest

indicators.note: round about means the letters of the word for release are turned and reordered

parts.note: to detach is to release or set free

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the city name is taken

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK

explanation.surface: A city lets go of half its centre for a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round about' turns the release word into DECATH; 'the capital' is London, the UK capital, and 'half' takes its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is an athletics competition of ten events.

clue.text: Return and raise the white flag

definitions.meaning: a financial return or profit on an investment

explanation.definitionFit: Yield means both a return on money and to give way or surrender.

clue.text: One delayed, possibly, repairing metal core. Hard lines!

indicators.note: repairing suggests putting the pieces of the two words back together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone running late blames a botched repair of a metal core, with a sympathetic 'hard luck' tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairing' rearranges METALCORE. 'Hard lines!' is a sympathetic aside to the person arriving late, adding no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held up may well turn up after the start, arriving behind the others.

clue.text: Frill sported by companion in a Parisian street

indicators.note: the companion is placed within the French street word

parts.note: rue is French for street
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A fancy ruffle is worn by someone's companion strolling along a street in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour is a British award, so CH can stand for a companion; 'sported by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a pleated or gathered strip of fabric used as trimming on clothes.

clue.text: Parking like 9. making an impression

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the solution at 9 across describes someone who is late

explanation.surface: Parking, just like a latecomer, leaves its mark somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 9 across, a person who arrives late, so 'like 9' gives LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A printing plate is the engraved surface that stamps an image on paper.

clue.text: Rose and fell almost disproportionately, a chap gathered

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: unduly means excessively, out of proportion
Ted is a typical man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: Something swelled and sank out of all proportion while a fellow collected it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims UNDULY to UNDUL; 'gathered' merely links the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that undulated moved up and down in waves, rising and falling.

clue.text: Oriental divine involved in footballer's nuptials

indicators.note: involved in means the first pieces are wrapped up inside the footballer

parts.note: a wing, or winger, is a footballer playing out on the flank
E stands for eastern, oriental
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine or cleric

explanation.surface: A clergyman from the East takes part in a football star's marriage ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: E and DD go inside WING. A divine is a theologian, so DD (Doctor of Divinity) stands for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials are a marriage ceremony, the plural noun matching the celebration it names.

clue.text: Cloak a Kentish doctor left inside after treatment?

annotationWithheld.why: Cloak a Kentish doctor left inside after treatment? (9): SE, MB and L account for SEMBL, but no reading of the clue gives the D, I, S, E that surround them
annotationWithheld.clue: Cloak a Kentish doctor left inside after treatment?

clue.text: Instant-retail English wine

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
to retail goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: A quick shop sale of a bottle of English wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Instant-retail' hides two separate pieces: MO and SELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the valley of the Moselle river in Germany.

clue.text: Horse damaged cable at edge of the Strand

indicators.note: damaged means the word horse is broken and rearranged

parts.note: a line is a cable or rope

explanation.surface: A horse damages a cable beside London's Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Strand' looks like the London street, but a strand is a beach. 'damaged' rearranges HORSE into SHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoreline is the line where land meets water, the boundary of a beach.

clue.text: Opponents have right to limit most old people's registration

parts.note: in bridge, East and North sit as opponents

indicators.note: to limit means the abbreviation for right encloses the next pieces
most means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: old as written, before trimming
men are people

explanation.surface: Rival parties are entitled to cap the number of elderly signing up.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, and East and North sit on opposing sides; 'to limit' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of signing up, putting one's name on a register.

clue.text: Fruit he thus rejected — outside not quite ready for eating

indicators.note: outside means the trimmed word sits around the turned pair
not quite means the final letter is cut from the synonym

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready for eating

indicators.note: rejected means the two words are thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A man spurns a piece of fruit that has not quite ripened enough to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns HE SO into OSEH; 'not quite' trims RIPE to RIP, which goes 'outside' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosehip is the berry-like seed pod of a rose bush, used for syrups and jellies.

clue.text: Flamboyance of glass seen around a church

indicators.note: seen around means the glass is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of glass

explanation.surface: Showiness of stained glass visible all round a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' tells you the glass encloses the article and the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is dash and stylish confidence.

clue.text: Vocalist turns treasure trove official's gold round

indicators.note: turns, with round, means the gold within the official's title is spun the other way

parts.note: in Britain a coroner holds inquests into finds of treasure trove
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A singer is said to switch around the gold belonging to an official who rules on buried treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns ... round' reverses the gold within the official's title, giving RO. In Britain a coroner rules on whether buried gold or silver found is treasure trove.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooner is a singer of sentimental songs in a soft, smooth style.

clue.text: Colour of animal carrying artist?

indicators.note: carrying means the animal bears the artist inside it

parts.note: a camel is a beast of burden
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: What shade is the beast of burden bearing a painter?
explanation.walkthrough: RA goes inside CAMEL; RA (Royal Academician) is the crossword shorthand for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a light golden-brown shade, named for burnt sugar.

clue.text: Morning drink always inhibited the old championship

indicators.note: inhibited means the poetic word for always holds the other pieces in check, around them

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe
an Open is a championship anyone may enter, as in golf

explanation.surface: A breakfast tipple has always held back a traditional sporting championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhibited' is the container signal: the poetic word for always holds the rest. The Open is the golf championship.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a stiff drink taken first thing to wake oneself up, chiefly American usage.

clue.text: Furnish with explosives, initially, before sally

indicators.note: before places the letter in front of the joke
initially means just the first letter of the word explosives is used

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: Equip with explosives first, ahead of a military sortie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sally' looks like a sortie by troops, but here it is a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to supply or fit out with what is needed.

clue.text: Little money for writer supported by church

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by puts the church below the writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Barely any cash for an author backed by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supported by' puts CE beneath PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence are the smallest British coins, a small sum of money.

clue.text: Like all animals, but some more than others?

definitions.meaning: alike, matching one another in amount or status

definitions.text: all animals, but some more than others?
definitions.meaning: Orwell's Animal Farm rule that every beast shares the same status, though some more so than the rest

explanation.definitionFit: Things that are alike match in value, and Orwell's pigs proclaimed every beast level but some more so than others.

clue.text: Perfect voice

definitions.meaning: complete, absolute, as in a total stranger

explanation.definitionFit: Utter means both absolute, as in utter nonsense, and to speak words.

clue.text: Endless suave and sophisticated pops

indicators.note: endless means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: urbane means smoothly polished and refined in manner

explanation.surface: Smooth, worldly fathers who never stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims URBANE. 'Pops' are fathers, and a pope is literally a papa, so 'pops' points to a papal name: eight popes have been called Urban.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope comes from papa, father, so 'pops' are pontiffs, and several pontiffs took the name Urban.

clue.text: Discussion group move to admit German with note

indicators.note: to admit means the verb for move lets the other pieces in, holding them inside

parts.note: to come is to move towards someone
mit is the German word for with
te is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Members of a debating panel propose letting in a German who brings a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' looks like a person being admitted, but it combines with 'with' to give the German word; 'to admit' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee is a body of people appointed to consider matters and report back.

clue.text: Unsystematic composition written before dinner, perhaps

indicators.note: written before puts the composition first, ahead of the meal

parts.note: a piece is a composition of music or writing
dinner is one example of a meal

explanation.surface: A random little work is drafted just ahead of an evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piecemeal means done bit by bit, haphazardly rather than to a plan.

clue.text: Bird carried back by detergent

indicators.note: back means the carried run of letters is read from right to left
carried means the letters sit within the cleaning word, borne along by it

explanation.surface: A wading bird is transported home by a packet of washing powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried' marks TERGE inside 'detergent', and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a long-legged wading species.
